selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main point is given in the opening example of the garden?
questions.answer: Different readers will benefit at different levels, and even if someone cannot grasp everything, he can still receive a meaningful share.

questions.question: Why is the image of people with longer arms included in the garden example?
questions.answer: It shows that some readers have greater capacity than others, and the work serves all of them, not just one kind.

questions.question: How does the second reason connect the subject of the book to its difficulty?
questions.answer: The book discusses the oneness of Allah in a very wide and deep way, so many readers cannot take in all of it at once.

questions.question: How is this writing method contrasted with many other books?
questions.answer: Other books are often written to fit the understanding of readers, but this one was not shaped that way.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of readers may struggle with that long method of proof?
questions.answer: People with limited understanding may find it hard to follow.

questions.question: In the third reason, why is keeping a truth unbroken so important?
questions.answer: Because separating it too much could weaken how clearly and fully it is conveyed.

questions.question: Why did the writer feel he should not reorganize or correct the work?
questions.answer: He felt the writing was not coming purely from his own choice, so changing it according to his own thoughts seemed unfitting.

questions.question: What effect can that many proofs have on the discussion?
questions.answer: It can make the discussion feel extended and difficult for some readers.

questions.question: What overall attitude does the passage teach readers to have before beginning this treatise?
questions.answer: Readers should be humble, patient, and ready to benefit as much as they can, even if they do not understand every part.

questions.question: What final conclusion can be drawn from the whole passage about why the treatise is difficult?
questions.answer: Its difficulty comes from a combination of profound subject matter, detailed proof, personal writing style, and challenging circumstances of composition.

questions.question: What reassurance is given to readers who may not understand the whole treatise?
questions.answer: They are told that no one will leave without gaining something from it.

questions.question: What hopeful point is still made for every reader?
questions.answer: Every reader can still receive some share of benefit.

questions.question: What does the garden image suggest about differences among readers?
questions.answer: It suggests that readers do not all have the same ability, but the work still has benefit for each of them.

questions.question: How does the second cause describe the treatment of Divine unity?
questions.answer: It describes it as presented in a very comprehensive way connected to a supreme divine manifestation.

questions.question: What subject is described as being presented in a highly comprehensive way?
questions.answer: The affirmation of Allah’s unity is presented in a very complete and far-reaching way.

questions.question: According to the third cause, what must often come before one proof?
questions.answer: Many preparatory explanations must come first.

questions.question: How does the fourth cause add another kind of difficulty beyond sentence length?
questions.answer: It shows that not only the wording but also the large number of proofs can make the discussion heavy for some readers.

questions.question: How did those conditions affect editing?
questions.answer: The first draft was not revised.

questions.question: What can a careful student learn from all five causes taken together?
questions.answer: The difficulty of the book comes from both the greatness of its message and the difficult conditions under which it was written.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the opening warning in this passage?
questions.answer: It prepares readers not to expect easy understanding of everything while still encouraging them to benefit.

questions.question: How does the garden example help a student approach a challenging religious text?
questions.answer: It teaches the student to take the amount he can reach and not become discouraged by what is beyond him.

questions.question: What is the basic idea of the first cause in simple words?
questions.answer: The book follows the writer’s own inner path of understanding instead of a commonly adjusted teaching style.

questions.question: Why might a work written mainly from personal understanding be harder for others?
questions.answer: Because it may not follow the patterns or explanations most readers expect.

questions.question: According to the third cause, why are introductory points needed before a proof?
questions.answer: They prepare the mind so the proof can be understood in its full meaning.
